output.brief:
Store 14's rise from 1.5% to 2.3% rests on interim estimates extrapolated from cycle counts. Those estimates carry roughly ±0.6 points of error per quarter. Across the chain, about half of stores that showed two consecutive rises of this size were not confirmed by the year-end full count. Store 14's past full counts were steady at 1.5–1.8%. The rise in recorded shoplifting incidents is also seen chain-wide, after a new incident app launched on 1 April, so it isn't good evidence of more theft at store 14. The ethics-line tip was checked against CCTV and was not substantiated. The sales mix hasn't changed, so that explanation is out. Self-checkout and the bus interchange are plausible but unproven. Neighbouring stores show no matching rise, but that doesn't settle which factor matters.

Next steps: keep store 14 in the 7 December full count. Don't pull the self-checkout lanes, hire a guard, or discipline anyone until that result is compared with the interim figures. Decline the proposal to skip the count, because it would remove the only reliable check. If the full count confirms a real rise, investigate causes then. I'm moderately confident in this.
